title: Relief Allowed Against a Restored Ridgecrest Advantage Premium Balance
content:
Credit adjustments standing on the premium account of a terminated Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment are allowed against the restored premium balance according to how many of them stand there.

**Where at least 2 credit adjustments stand on the premium account**, the relief allowed against it is every credit adjustment posted on the account in the contract year, whatever reason each of them carries.

**Where exactly 1 credit adjustment stands on the premium account**, the relief allowed against it is the credit adjustments posted on the account in the last 3 months, whatever reason each of them carries.

**Where no credit adjustment stands on the premium account**, the relief allowed against it is nothing.

The billing cadence of the enrollment does not come into this: the count of credit adjustments standing on the premium account is the whole of the test. The reason each credit adjustment carries makes no difference either.

*A premium account carrying 2 credit adjustments, of 35.00 USD posted this month and 40.00 USD posted eight months ago in the same contract year.* At least 2 stand there, so the relief allowed is both of them, together 75.00 USD.

*A premium account carrying exactly 1 credit adjustment of 40.00 USD posted eight months ago.* The relief allowed is the credit adjustments posted in the last 3 months, and that one falls outside them, so the relief allowed is nothing.

*A premium account carrying no credit adjustment.* The relief allowed against the restored premium balance is nothing.
